title: Import a fleet
subtitle: Bring an existing Coolify or Dokploy instance into Tugra — its apps, domains and config. Nothing on the source is changed.
sourceCoolifyHint: Connect with a Coolify API token to preview everything it is running.
sourceDokployHint: Connect with a Dokploy API key to preview all of its projects.
localDockerHint: Adopting plain Docker containers instead? Use "Discover" on a server's page.
tokenHint: Create the token on your admin/owner team with the read ability (add read:sensitive too — it's used at apply time to fetch env values, container labels and Dockerfile text). A 403 means Coolify's API "Allowed IPs" setting is on and doesn't include this hub's IP; add it there or clear the list.
tokenHintDokploy: Create the key in Dokploy under Profile, API/CLI. Use an owner or admin key so every project is visible. It is also used at apply time for env values, database credentials and basic-auth passwords. Enter the panel address only; the API path is added for you.
servicesImported: {count} service stack(s) will be imported as stopped compose apps (nothing is deployed):
targetHint: Where the imported apps and database records are created. Database DATA is moved by the separate migrator step; app volume data is copied manually.
noTarget: Add a server to this team first, then come back to import.
rollbackBody: Removes the apps this import created on the target server. Apps you have deployed since are kept. This cannot be undone.
coverageDeferred: Custom labels and Dockerfile text are read when you apply.
migrateDesc: Your databases were recreated empty. Generate a one-time command and run it on your source ({source}) host to copy each database's data into its new Tugra database. The token works once and expires.
migrateTokenOnce: Copy this now — the token is shown only once.
migrateActive: A migration command is active until {date}.
remapTitle: Point apps at their new databases
remapDesc: Rewrite each migrated app's environment so it connects to its new Tugra database instead of the old {source} one. Preview the exact (secret-masked) changes first, then apply — changes take effect on each app's next deploy, and an undo is available.
remapNoLink: Won't auto-link the database network ({reason}) — wire it by hand
remapApplyBody: Rewrites the shown environment keys on each app. Changes take effect on the next deploy and can be undone.
remapApplied: Environment rewritten — redeploy each app to apply
reason_label_reserved_traefik: in the reserved traefik.* namespace (owned by Tugra's ingress routing and would hijack shared proxy routes)
reason_label_reserved_tugra: in the reserved tugra.* namespace (Tugra's own bookkeeping labels)
reason_label_reserved_compose: in the reserved com.docker.compose.* namespace (Docker Compose project/service identity)
reason_label_reserved_swarm: in the reserved com.docker.swarm.* namespace (Docker Swarm service identity)
reason_label_reserved_stack: in the reserved com.docker.stack.* namespace (Docker stack identity)
reason_trigger_tag: tag-triggered deploys have no Tugra equivalent (push only) — auto-deploy turned off
reason_watch_paths_invalid: a pattern is not a valid Tugra watch-path glob — none carried
reason_limits_invalid: CPU/memory limits are outside Tugra's accepted range — none carried
reason_command_compose: a compose app declares its command in its compose file
reason_command_invalid: the command/args are not valid for Tugra's exec-form override
reason_dockerfile_not_build: inline Dockerfile applies only to Dockerfile builds
reason_dockerfile_too_large: the Dockerfile is larger than 48 KiB
reason_dockerfile_nul: Dockerfile must not contain a NUL byte
reason_dockerfile_not_from: the first instruction of the Dockerfile must be FROM (only ARG may precede it)
reason_dockerfile_no_from: the Dockerfile has no FROM instruction
reason_dockerfile_invalid: the Dockerfile text is not valid
reason_dockerfile_rejected: Tugra would not accept the Dockerfile text
reason_build_target_invalid: the build target is not a valid Dockerfile stage name
reason_build_target_not_dockerfile: a build target applies only to Dockerfile builds
reason_labels_compose: compose apps declare labels in the compose file
reason_access_control_dropped: an access-control middleware label (basic auth / IP allow-list / forward auth) was not carried; the imported app is not gated by it until you recreate it with Tugra basic auth or IP rules, before the first deploy
reason_context_path: Tugra has no separate docker build context (base directory only)
reason_static_spa: Tugra's static builds always serve an SPA fallback
reason_replicas: replicas convert the app to a swarm service — set the replica count explicitly in Tugra after import
reason_domain_dns01: uses a DNS-01 certificate — needs a DNS-provider credential binding in Tugra; it will use Let's Encrypt HTTP-01 once DNS points here
reason_domain_custom_cert: uses an uploaded certificate — upload it in Tugra (the certificate itself is not carried yet)
reason_domain_no_https: was served without HTTPS — Tugra serves custom domains over HTTPS (Let's Encrypt) and will upgrade it
reason_domain_redirect: redirects to {to} — configure the redirect in Tugra
reason_domain_service_not_compose: targets a named service, but this is not a compose app — Tugra routes the single app container
reason_domain_path_invalid: the path is not a valid Tugra path prefix — served at the host root
reason_domain_dup_route: same host with a different path/port/service — Tugra serves one route per host
reason_domain_host_invalid: not a hostname Tugra can serve
reason_domain_alias: is the www/bare counterpart of the primary domain — Tugra already serves it there
reason_domain_service_no_port: no routing port on the source — add this service domain in Tugra
reason_domain_service_path: per-service domains have no path routing in Tugra — add it manually
reason_domain_service_name_invalid: not a valid compose service name
reason_domain_service_limit: Tugra allows at most {max} service domains
reason_domain_port_differs: routes to container port {port}, but Tugra serves one container port per app ({primaryPort})
reason_domain_path_differs: uses a different path than the primary domain — Tugra's path prefix is app-wide
reason_domain_extra_limit: Tugra allows at most {max} extra domains
reason_domain_primary_service: bound to compose service "{service}" — Tugra routes the primary domain to the web service it infers from the compose file; verify it
reason_ports_compose: a compose app declares its published ports in its compose file
reason_port_is_ingress: container port {port} is the HTTP ingress port, already served through the proxy — publish it on the host manually if it is needed
reason_port_duplicate: host port + protocol already published by another mapping
reason_ports_limit: Tugra allows at most {max} extra published ports
reason_redirects_invalid: some redirect rules are not valid in Tugra (single-line regex/replacement, max 1024 chars) — re-create them manually
reason_redirects_limit: Tugra allows at most {max} redirect rules
reason_setting_rejected: Tugra rejected the setting — set it manually
reason_inline_dockerfile_rejected: Tugra rejected the setting. Set it manually
reason_extras_read_failed: could not read this app's labels or Dockerfile from the source; set them manually
reason_labels_unparsable: the label block could not be parsed
reason_ingress_uninterpretable: the source ingress could not be interpreted — configure domains and ports manually
reason_basic_auth_not_carried: basic-auth not carried — re-protect the app before cutover
reason_basic_auth_users_dropped: some basic-auth users could not be stored in Tugra — re-add them before cutover
reason_custom_labels_deferred: read when you apply: Tugra-safe labels are carried; reserved ones (traefik.*, tugra.*, com.docker.*) cannot be and are named in the import timeline
reason_dockerfile_deferred: read when you apply and set as the app's inline Dockerfile
reason_coolify_basic_auth: the source gated this app with HTTP basic auth; the credentials are not read, so the imported app is NOT gated until you set basic auth in Tugra before the first deploy
reason_coolify_published_ports: host-published ports are not carried; add them in the app's Ports settings
reason_coolify_docker_options: custom Docker run options are owner-gated in Tugra and never auto-applied
reason_coolify_deploy_hooks: set them in the app's Deploy hooks after import
reason_coolify_limits: resource limits are not carried from Coolify yet; set them in Tugra
reason_coolify_build_target: build target not carried from Coolify yet
reason_coolify_watch_paths: watch paths not carried from Coolify yet
reason_coolify_inline_dockerfile: an inline-Dockerfile app has no git repository; Tugra builds Dockerfile apps from a repo, so this app cannot be imported yet (repo-less Dockerfile apps are a planned feature)
reason_dokploy_registry: the registry credential is not carried; add the registry in Tugra before deploying a private image
reason_dokploy_build_secrets: build secret values are not read; re-add them as Tugra build secrets
reason_dokploy_swarm_labels: Dokploy Swarm service labels are not carried (Tugra custom labels are container labels)
reason_dokploy_domains: preview or disabled domains are not carried

blockers.title: Variables that cannot be carried
blockers.body: These apps have variables Tugra cannot read or that are not valid environment names. Fix the source (or the token) and re-run the plan, or acknowledge to create the app without them.

tokenReadOnly.title: The API token cannot read variable values
tokenReadOnly.body: These apps cannot be imported: create a Coolify token with the read:sensitive ability and reconnect.

env.ackWarning: These apps will be created WITHOUT these variables, and a deploy may fail or misbehave.

remap.serviceLinkReview: points at an old service (e.g. MinIO); set the new endpoint after migrating its data

git.title: Git repositories
git.body: Private repositories are linked to the connected GitHub/Gitea source that can actually see them. Connect a GitHub App once, then re-check: every app it covers is linked in one step.
git.loading: Checking which connected sources can see each repository…

group.needsSource: No connected source can see these
group.ambiguous: Several sources can see these (pick one after import)

git.relinkBody: Link the imported apps that a connected source can now see.
git.sshConverted: SSH URL will be converted to https

deployKey.title: Add this public deploy key to the repository

git.gitlabNote: GitLab and Bitbucket sources are not supported yet. These repositories are created unlinked.

services.title: Service stacks
services.desc: Each Coolify service becomes one stopped Tugra compose app built from the service's own compose file. Secrets are carried, never regenerated, and nothing is deployed until you do it.
services.previewFailed: Could not read the service details
services.needsTarget: This service runs on the source's own host: choose its target server.

compat.template: An app-store template exists; imported with its own compose

volume.hostBind: Host folder, carried as a named volume

domain.none: No domain is mapped: the service stays private and joins a private network.

hold.label: Created stopped
hold.why: Running it next to the source would split live traffic. Stop the source and repoint its routes by hand first.

env.unavailable: The token cannot read this service's variables (it needs read:sensitive). Needed: {names}

image.unpinned: {services} run a floating tag. Pin the version the source runs, or the registry's latest is pulled.

risk.compose-unavailable: The source did not return the compose file.
risk.compose-unparsed: The compose file could not be read.
risk.gate: The safety gate refuses something in the compose; it is never carried or overridden.
risk.volume-name: A volume has a name the data step cannot address.
risk.volume-hostbind: A host folder is carried as a named volume.
risk.volume-size-unknown: The size of the data is not measured yet.
risk.image-floating: An image runs a floating tag.
risk.files-needed: Config files are needed from the source.
risk.data-manual-large: A volume is too large for the hub copy: copy it by hand.
risk.data-not-carried: Some data is intentionally not carried.
risk.hold: Created stopped and held until you repoint its routes.
risk.deploy-manual: Created stopped: you deploy it yourself.
risk.reach: No domain is mapped: other apps must be repointed.
risk.container-name: The container name is not carried.
risk.secrets-unverified: Variables are read from the source when you apply.
risk.type-unsupported: Not imported: every member needs something Tugra never carries.

checklist.title: Next steps for {name}
checklist.deploy-after-data: Nothing was deployed. Copy the data first, then deploy {name} yourself.
checklist.data-step: Copy the data of {volumes} into the new volume(s) before the first deploy.
checklist.quiesce: Stop the source ({members}) while you copy: a live copy of an embedded database is not crash-consistent.
checklist.tunnel: Stop the source connector and repoint the Cloudflare public-hostname origins by hand before you start {name}. Running both splits live traffic.
checklist.repoint-dependents: Apps that used {name}'s old internal host must be repointed to its new address.
checklist.unpinned-image: {services} run a floating image tag: pin the version the source runs.
checklist.reach: {name} is private. Join network {network} and use the name {alias} to reach it.
checklist.reachManual: {name} is private. No network was attached: add one in the app's network settings.
